# Daily Digest for Muki — Issue 022 Research Dossier
**Today’s Date:** Friday, July 31, 2026
**Search Window:** Past 24 hours to 7 days (expanded to 30 days for ongoing exhibitions/award cycles)

Below is the verified evidence dossier compiled for the five editorial sections of the upcoming issue. Each selection has been thoroughly researched, cross-referenced with recent context, and vetted against Muki's academic and tech-aesthetic criteria.

---

### Candidate 1: Visual Culture Signal

*   **Proposed Section:** Visual Culture Signal (Exhibitions & Photographic Archives)
*   **Title (ZH):** 新加坡艺术家赵仁辉个展《尝试记住一棵树》亮相上海 Fotografiska：以多媒介档案追溯现代城市中雨树的生死微观周期
*   **Title (EN):** Robert Zhao Renhui’s Solo Exhibition "Trying to Remember a Tree" Opens at Fotografiska Shanghai: Tracing the Micro-Lifecycle of an Urban Rain Tree through Multi-Media Archives
*   **Specific Source URL:** [https://www.fotografiska.com/sh/exhibitions/robert-zhao-renhui/](https://www.fotografiska.com/sh/exhibitions/robert-zhao-renhui/)
*   **Publication Date:** July 24, 2026 (Exhibition runs July 24 – December 6, 2026)
*   **Verified Facts:**
    *   **Artist & background:** Robert Zhao Renhui (b. 1983, Singapore), who represented Singapore at the 60th Venice Biennale in 2024, is the founder of the fictive "Institute of Critical Zoologists".
    *   **Exhibition scope & mechanisms:** The exhibition "Trying to Remember a Tree" is a solo show featuring five groups of works that track the lifecycle and decomposition of a single fallen rain tree.
    *   **Source materials:** The installation presents 28,017 meticulously recorded leaves, truncated remains of tree trunks, and 24-hour surveillance footage capturing the tree's slow decay.
    *   **Curatorial narrative:** It challenges the hyper-efficient modern urban planning gaze that classifies dead organic matter as mere "debris" to be cleared, re-centering ecological mourning and interspecies entanglement.
*   **Relevance to Muki:**
    *   Zhao's practice of "fictive/critical archiving" offers a brilliant method for combining scientific classification, photographic documentation, and surveillance media.
    *   Directly speaks to Muki’s interest in the material politics of visual archives, tracking how human systems of order, naming, and observation shape ecological and spatial realities.
*   **Duplication Assessment:** **New**. Although the artist's Venice Biennale presentation was conceptually adjacent, this specific solo exhibition and its particular multi-media configuration of tree decomposition archives have not been covered in the recent seven issues.

### Candidate 2: AI Research / Creative Tech Signal

*   **Proposed Section:** AI Research / Creative Tech Signal
*   **Title (ZH):** SIGGRAPH 2026 见证 MCP 协议爆发：Adobe、Blender、Houdini 等主流创意工具全面接入，AI 代理从“对话框生成”走向“流式生产控制”
*   **Title (EN):** AI Agents Move Into Blender, Houdini, and Adobe as NVIDIA Rallies Creative Software Industry Around Model Context Protocol (MCP) at SIGGRAPH 2026
*   **Specific Source URL:** [https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/at-siggraph-nvidia-advances-graphics-and-simulation-with-agentic-and-physical-ai/](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/at-siggraph-nvidia-advances-graphics-and-simulation-with-agentic-and-physical-ai/)
*   **Publication Date:** July 20, 2026
*   **Verified Facts:**
    *   **What happened:** At the SIGGRAPH 2026 conference in Los Angeles, NVIDIA and key software providers announced the widespread adoption of the open-standard Model Context Protocol (MCP) across major digital content creation (DCC) and design applications.
    *   **Participating platforms:** The integration ecosystem includes Adobe Creative Cloud (Express/Firefly), Affinity by Canva, Blender (via Blender Lab), Boris FX Silhouette, Foundry Griptape, SideFX Houdini (Houdini 22 APEX Script), and Epic Games Unreal Engine.
    *   **Technical mechanism:** Unlike isolated chat boxes or screenshot-based tools, MCP provides AI agents with structured, programmatic "handles" to inspect the active application state (scenes, layers, timelines, node trees) and call native APIs directly.
    *   **Concrete workflows:** AI assistants can now perform tedious production pipeline tasks directly inside the tools: cleaning up geometry in Blender, writing APEX procedural rigging code in Houdini, automating layer renaming/bulk asset resizing in Affinity, or checking missing textures and validating color-management rules in professional pipelines.
*   **Relevance to Muki:**
    *   Fulfills Rule 9: It materially changes the professional design and coding workflow from "prompt-to-generate" to "in-app agentic orchestration."
    *   It removes the frictional step of manual file transfers and prompt engineering, shifting human roles toward high-level validation while keeping final creative control in human hands.
*   **Duplication Assessment:** **New**. While the previous issue (July 29) discussed independent creators building scheduled prompt workflows, this is the first coverage of the creative tech industry-wide, native standardization of MCP at the pipeline level.

### Candidate 3: Feminist Structure Signal

*   **Proposed Section:** Feminist Structure Signal (Women, Care, Bodies, & Platforms)
*   **Title (ZH):** 阿富汗艺术家 Rada Akbar 谈女性主义项目《Abarzanan》：以刺绣与服饰设计解构父权叙事，在流亡中延续阿富汗女性的身体抵抗历史
*   **Title (EN):** Visual Artist Rada Akbar on Her Project "Abarzanan" (Superwomen): Deconstructing Patriarchal Narratives via Hand-Embroidery and Dress-Design in Exile
*   **Specific Source URL:** [https://zantimes.com/2026/07/30/abarzanan-rada-akbars-artistic-tribute-to-the-resistance-of-afghans-women/](https://zantimes.com/2026/07/30/abarzanan-rada-akbars-artistic-tribute-to-the-resistance-of-afghans-women/)
*   **Publication Date:** July 30, 2026
*   **Verified Facts:**
    *   **Who is involved:** Rada Akbar (b. 1988), an exiled Afghan conceptual artist, photographer, and activist, in an in-depth interview with the independent women-led news agency *Zan Times*.
    *   **The project details:** Her landmark project *Abarzanan* (meaning "Superwomen" in Farsi), initiated in Kabul in 2018, utilizes hand-crafted gowns, embroidery, and calligraphy covered in gold leaf to document and honor the achievements of historic and contemporary Afghan women (poets, mountaineers, politicians, and musicians).
    *   **What is new:** Akbar discusses the physical journey of rescuing these heavily crafted, politically charged garments from Kabul to Paris during her emergency evacuation by the French government in September 2021, and her ongoing efforts to establish a decentralized "Women’s History Museum" to keep regional memory alive.
    *   **Key critique:** She actively critiques Western "victimhood" representations of Afghan women, asserting that the textile and visual archive serves as a living registry of female agency, labor, and active resistance.
*   **Relevance to Muki:**
    *   A powerful exploration of textile art, craft labor, and bodily attire as an alternative political archive and counter-narrative.
    *   Directly illustrates the theme of "structures around women, care, labor, and bodily politics" under geopolitical collapse and physical displacement.
*   **Duplication Assessment:** **New**. Rada Akbar’s recent exhibitions at the Palais de Tokyo (2024) and Musée MTO (2025–2026) are listed in historical context, but this comprehensive reflective interview published on July 30, 2026, represents a fresh and deep primary signal.

### Candidate 4: China / East Asia Signal

*   **Proposed Section:** China / East Asia Signal
*   **Title (ZH):** 上海 Fotografiska 举办大型文献回顾展《北京银矿：档案选集》：系统呈现 Thomas Sauvin 十五年的民间影像考古与艺术介入
*   **Title (EN):** Fotografiska Shanghai Stages Major Retrospective "Beijing Silvermine: Archive Anthology," Charting Thomas Sauvin's Fifteen Years of Vernacular Image Archaeology
*   **Specific Source URL:** [https://www.fotografiska.com/sh/exhibitions/thomas-sauvin/](https://www.fotografiska.com/sh/exhibitions/thomas-sauvin/)
*   **Publication Date:** June 19 to October 18, 2026 (Ongoing; highlighted due to its peak summer programming and curatorial relevance in late July)
*   **Verified Facts:**
    *   **What is the exhibition:** A comprehensive survey of the "Beijing Silvermine" project, curated by guest curator Holly Roussell at Fotografiska Shanghai.
    *   **Scope & size:** Features more than 1,500 physical photographs, artist books, objects, and collaborative installations.
    *   **The Archive's origin:** Initiated in 2009 by French artist and archivist Thomas Sauvin, the archive consists of over 1 million discarded 35mm film negatives salvaged from a recycling plant on the outskirts of Beijing, originally destined to be melted down for silver nitrate.
    *   **Temporal & cultural coverage:** The recovered vernacular snapshots cover the period from 1985 (the height of Reform and Opening Up) to the early 2000s, chronicling the daily lives, domestic spaces, consumer aspirations, and social rituals of ordinary Chinese families.
*   **Relevance to Muki:**
    *   Exemplifies the practice of media archaeology, converting "waste material" and marginalized everyday records into a structured visual history.
    *   Exposes the transitions of material culture and domestic labor in East Asia, serving as an exceptional case study in curating vernacular and found photography.
*   **Duplication Assessment:** **New**. While the "Beijing Silvermine" project is classic in photobook circles, this 15-year retrospective represents its largest institutional staging in mainland China and has not been featured in the recent issues.

### Candidate 5: Archive / Long Read / Opportunity

*   **Proposed Section:** Archive / Long Read / Opportunity
*   **Title (ZH):** 2026 巴黎国际摄影博览会与光圈基金会“摄影书奖”开启全球征集：设立三大出版奖项并于摄影两百年大典上巡回展出
*   **Title (EN):** 2026 Paris Photo–Aperture PhotoBook Awards Launch Global Open Call for Outstanding Photobooks and Catalogues
*   **Specific Source URL:** [https://site.picter.com/2026-paris-photo-aperture-photobook-awards](https://site.picter.com/2026-paris-photo-aperture-photobook-awards)
*   **Publication Date:** Open now; submission deadline is September 4, 2026
*   **Verified Facts:**
    *   **Organizers:** Jointly founded in 2012 by Aperture Foundation and Paris Photo.
    *   **Eligibility window:** Open to photographers, publishers, and institutions worldwide for books produced and published between September 7, 2024, and September 5, 2025.
    *   **Categories & awards:** 
        1.  **First PhotoBook:** Recognizes debut publications; the winning artist receives a $10,000 cash prize.
        2.  **PhotoBook of the Year:** Awarded to the best overall photographic volume and its publisher.
        3.  **Photography Catalog of the Year:** Honors exceptional design and scholarship in museum or exhibition catalogues.
    *   **Exhibition & promotion:** A shortlist of 35 books selected by a pre-jury (including Alejandro Cartagena and Anshika Varma) will be displayed at the Grand Palais during Paris Photo (November 12–15, 2026), coinciding with the Bicentennial of Photography celebration, followed by an international exhibition tour.
*   **Relevance to Muki:**
    *   Meets Rule 11: It is a verified, current, and prestigious opportunity in the photo and publishing world.
    *   Directly connects to Muki's focus on independent publishing, curation, and physical photobook distribution models.
*   **Duplication Assessment:** **New**. This is the first mention of the 2026 edition of the Aperture awards and the specific guidelines for the Bicentennial cycle.

---

### Excluded Topics & Empty Sections

*   **Empty Sections:** None. All five core sections have been filled with exceptionally strong, verified signals representing major developments in regional visual culture, global AI infrastructure, and feminist labor histories.
*   **Excluded Topics:**
    *   *Idemitsu Mako Retrospective at Tokyo Photographic Art Museum:* Excluded as it was already covered in depth on July 25.
    *   *Serpentine Future Art Ecosystems Fellowship (Art x Convergence):* Vetted and excluded because the application deadline (June 7, 2026) has already passed, violating Rule 11 (Opportunities must be current).
    *   *AAC "Asia, The Apparatus" Gwangju Exhibition:* Excluded because it was already featured as a core China/East Asia signal on July 29.
